core.title: Populate the Graph Context section of every parent issue body
core.given: You are authoring or editing the body of an ATDD parent issue
core.when: you write or save the issue body
core.then: The body carries a Graph Context section populated with where the issue sits in the dependency graph — not missing and not left as the unexpanded injection placeholder.
prefer: Fill the Graph Context section with the issue's actual position in the dependency graph before work starts.
avoid: Omitting the Graph Context section from a parent issue body.
Leaving the injection placeholder in place of real graph-context content.
Filling the section with filler text just to satisfy the check without stating the issue's graph position.
core.why: A populated Graph Context section forces each issue to state where it sits in the dependency graph before work starts.
evidence: The parent-issue-body graph-context check passes for the issue body (the stack realization names the concrete validator).
A reviewer sees a Graph Context section in the parent issue body with non-placeholder content describing its dependency-graph position.
verification: Scope: the target of the check is the body of an ATDD parent issue — not a sub-issue, a comment, or a non-ATDD issue.

The check fails when the Graph Context section is absent from the parent issue body or still equals the unexpanded injection placeholder; the exact placeholder form is defined by the realization's issue template.

The automated check covers only section presence and placeholder replacement; whether the content genuinely states the issue's position in the dependency graph (no filler text) is judged by review, not by the check.
Severity 3; disposition suppress-and-clean (existing violations may be suppressed but must be cleaned); suppression deadline 2026-12-31.

fires: The planner drafts a new ATDD parent issue body.
The planner edits an existing ATDD parent issue body whose Graph Context section is missing.
An ATDD parent issue body still contains the graph-context injection placeholder instead of real content.
The planner edits any other part of an ATDD parent issue body that already has a populated Graph Context section (in scope; already satisfied as long as the section stays populated).
The task wording mentions none of the hint terms but the edit targets an ATDD parent issue body (task terms are non-gating hints).
doesNotFire: Editing a sub-issue, a comment, or a non-ATDD issue — anything that is not the body of an ATDD parent issue.
Editing plan documents or other plan artifacts (work-breakdown plans, acceptance definitions) that are not a parent issue body.

neutralityNotes: This convention is methodology-level, not stack-level: the ATDD parent issue body, its Graph Context section and the injection placeholder belong to the ATDD issue template, so the core names no stack, runtime, path or file kind and needs no structure-profile value — profileRequirements and proposedKeys are empty. The exact placeholder token is not spelled out in bun.json; the core defers its form to the realization's issue template (core verification). In doesNotFire, the ATDD-Bun artifact names 'wagons' and 'WMBTs' were generalized to 'work-breakdown plan artifacts'; the concrete names remain visible in bun.json, the delivered reference example. Validator/test ids, term ids and the agent-harness observer wiring are bunOnly. The suppression deadline 2026-12-31 is kept in core:verification because it is part of this rule's disposition, which stays with the rule rather than the profile.
